McLarty Mazda of Little Rock — new sales & service facility

Set: Orig Plans 10.16.2025 PRELIMINARY · BCO+H Architects · 35 sheets (Cover, LS, A1–A6)Systems: Pittco TMW 450 / TMW 450 EFG (legend SF-1 "curtain wall") · TMS 114XTFG (SF-2 "storefront") · EMS 114 interior · ½" frameless · black #63Glass: 1" Solarban 72 Acuity low-iron IG · ¼" / ½" clear tempered interiorSpecs: none in set (flagged)Scale: schedule drawings ¼" = 1'-0", plans/elevations ⅛" = 1'-0" (vector-snapped)

Considered & excluded (5 OH doors, 4 Rytec, 2 grilles)
Result against Martin's markups: 86 of 91 scope objects he marked were found blind (94.5%) with 0 false scope: all 16 exterior frames, all 6 exterior glazing-only items, the 3 interior storefront frames, 4 interior glazing-only items, all 24 frameless openings, the break metal, note 10, the A2.0 legend rows and all 15 detail titles he marked. Missed: the two glass rows in the A3.1 interior finish legend, finish note 13 on A3.0, and his silicone-joint and polished-edge counts. Sizes matched his Areas within an inch after one rounding bug was fixed (type 1). The comparison also exposed that bug and a region bug in the detail finder — both now fixed in the code.

Convention differences (not scope)

  • Plan A1.2: Martin highlights the tag hexagon (same as me) AND draws a Polylength along the opening with its length (Ext SF / Ext CW / Int SF / All Glass Wall Polylength). I drew tag highlights only — I could not snap opening boxes on this reference plan.
  • Elevations A2.0: Martin places one Area per frame; at 30/31a/31b he drew a single 29'-0" x 10'-4" Area across the three types. I drew one per type.
  • Schedule A3.2/A3.3: Martin highlights the whole type drawing in the system color, plus the hardware table; one Qty box ('3 Thus' at 24–26); Length Measurements on 30/31a/31b/32. I used Qty boxes on every type.
  • Martin leaves overhead doors, Rytec doors, grilles and HM-only doors blank; I marked them red (considered and excluded) on plan and elevation.
  • Martin used Ext SF for type 8 (TMW 450 door frame); I classed every TMW 450 as Ext CW because the A2.0 legend calls SF-1 'curtain wall'. Every other TMW 450 type he also marked Ext CW, so the legend rule held except for the single door frame.
  • Martin measured the frost band with the Glass Handrail Area tool; the subject map should treat that as film area on this job.
  • Martin marked 15 detail titles on the 6 detail/section sheets in his set; I marked 70 titles/callouts across 19 sheets, 7 of which (A5.4–A5.9, A5.13, A6.1) are not in his set.

What I changed after looking

  • A2.0 1 — Blind run snapped type 1 on the north elevation at 12'-3" and raised a false 'elevation vs schedule' RFI. Cause: a rounding bug in my feet-inch formatter wrote the schedule width as 13'-12.0", which parsed back as 12'-0", so the elevation matcher preferred the wrong rectangle. Martin's Area reads 14'-4 1/2"; after the fix the snap reads 14'-4.5" (schedule 14'-0"). The RFI was withdrawn.
  • A3.2 21 — I described the 14'-0" x 4'-0" HM window as 4 lites from a nearby '(4 EQUAL PANELS)' string that belongs to another type. The vector mullion count says 3 lites (4'-5" / 4'-6" / 4'-5"); Martin drew 3. Text was wrong, geometry was right.
  • A4.2 DET 6/A4.2 — Detail 6 (storefront jamb) was not found blind: my detail-region builder treated detail 7 (to the right) as 'above' and cut the region. Fixed the column test; detail 6 now hits 'STOREFRONT PER SCHEDULE'. Martin marked it.
  • A3.1 A3.1 SF-3 — Interior finish legend row SF-3 INTERIOR GLAZING — full-height frameless panels, 3M Fasara frost 36" AFF, black/clear silicone notes, 'local glass contractor'. I keyword-counted GLASS on A3.1 but never parsed the legend rows. Martin colored it.
  • A3.1 A3.1 D-8 — Finish legend row D-8 INTERIOR GLASS DOOR 36" x 84", frosted to 36", polished chrome trim, by local glass contractor. Same miss as SF-3.
  • A3.0 A3.0 note 13 — Finish note 13: 'All frameless glass hardware to be polished aluminum; top and bottom trim 2" thick max.' A scope note for the all-glass package. Not in my keyword list.
  • A3.2 HW tables — Martin highlights each door type's HARDWARE table in the system color (types 1, 3, 5, 8, 30, 31a, 31b, 32 on A3.2; 101 on A3.3). I marked only the general hardware schedule.
  • A3.3 FROST area — Martin measures the 36" frost band as an Area on every frameless type (24 areas, drawn with the Glass Handrail Area tool). I carried the film as one implied line item (qty 23) with no square footage.
  • A3.3 Counts — Martin places count symbols on each frameless type: SSG Caulk Count (76 silicone joints), Polished Edge Count (58 exposed edges), All Glass Doors (8). I had the door count only inside the descriptions and did not count joints or edges.
  • A1.2 21 callout — Martin adds a 'Hollow Metal' callout at the type 21 window on the plan so the estimator knows the frame is by others.

Mine only — judgment calls

  • Bi-fold door pairs at types 1, 3, 5 carried as pass-thru items (bifold/auto-door sub) with frame prep by us.
  • Mirrors: 6 x 18" x 36" frameless plate glass (toilet accessory 8, no manufacturer) — flagged glazier vs accessory package.
  • GF-1 gradient film at the type 3 upper band — marked at A3.2 and in the A2.0 legend; RFI on DF-1/GF-1 naming.
  • 24 ga pre-finished sill flashing under curtain wall sills (7 wall sections) — flagged for trade.
  • Door & frame note 12 (push bars at 1, 3, 5, 32) and the general hardware schedule.
  • RFIs: types 24–26 width 8'-0" (schedule) vs 7'-0" (elevation); narrow vs medium stile (legend vs schedule); film extent.
  • Glazing details on A5.4–A5.9, A5.13 and the mirror section on A6.1 (outside the 12-sheet bid set).

What this test shows

This set has no storefront schedule, and the method still worked. The key here was two pictorial door-and-frame schedules (A3.2, A3.3): every opening is drawn at ¼" scale with a circled mark, dimension strings, a description block and a hardware table. Reading those two sheets first — mark, description text, snapped frame rectangle, dimension strings — gave the complete mark list (34 exterior, 48 interior) with system, glass, size and door before any plan or elevation was opened. The plan then showed every hexagon tag exactly once (82 tags, matched to vector hexagons, so room numbers and revision triangles were not confused with door marks), and the elevations gave a second measurement of each exterior frame that agreed with the schedule except where the drawings themselves disagree (24–26).

What was different from Valvoline:

  1. The legend contradicts trade usage. A2.0 calls the 4½" TMW 450 "SF-1 curtain wall" and the TMS 114 "SF-2 storefront". I classified by the legend and flagged it; Martin did the same on every TMW 450 frame except the single door frame (type 8). The rule "legend wins, flag it" held.
  2. Interior all-glass is a different takeoff. 24 frameless openings are where most of Martin's 428 markups live: an Area per opening, an Area for the 36" frost band, a count symbol on every silicone joint (76) and every polished edge (58), a door count (8) and a Polylength per opening on the plan. I found and sized every opening and carried film, doors and polished edges as text, but I did not produce the joint and edge counts. Those are derivable from the same vector geometry (panel lines = joints; free edges = polished edges) and belong in the all-glass part of Frame Builder.
  3. Interior finish legends hold glazing rows. A3.1 rows SF-3 (interior glazing) and D-8 (interior glass door) and A3.0 note 13 were my only true misses. The fix is the same legend-row parser as A2.0, run on every schedule/legend sheet, not just the exterior one.
  4. Two code bugs surfaced only because of the comparison. A feet-inch rounding bug (13'-12.0" → 12'-0") made the elevation matcher pick the wrong rectangle at type 1 and raise a false RFI; a column test in the detail finder dropped detail 6/A4.2. Both were invisible in the blind result and obvious next to Martin's marks. That is the case for keeping every accept/reject logged: the diffs are the test suite.
  5. Plan opening lengths. Martin draws a Polylength along each opening on the plan; I highlighted tags only because the reference plan has no clean glass line to snap. The length is already known from the schedule and elevation, so the markup writer can place it along the wall at the tag without new vision work.

Cost: nothing in this takeoff needed a vision model. Sheet index, legend rows, schedule descriptions, type-drawing snaps, tag counts, elevation snaps, detail keyword search and the trade rules are all text and geometry. The model's job was deciding the rules once (legend vs trade, pass-thru, what a finish-legend row means), not reading 35 sheets.

What to build from this: the pictorial-schedule reader (mark → description → frame snap → dims); a legend-row parser run on every A3.x legend; tag detection by enclosing hexagon; the elevation matcher with schedule-size scoring (now with the rounding fix); the all-glass measures (joints, edges, film band); the Polylength-on-plan writer; and the scope-object scorer, which gave 94.5% here where a rectangle scorer would have scored this takeoff in the 30s against 428 count symbols.
